dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent from Whissle. Can you please tell me about the skin lesion or concern that brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I've got this red, crusty sore on the shaft of my penis that just won't go away. I have a very similar looking spot on my left middle finger too. They don't actually hurt, but the treatments I tried back home for syphilis and eczema didn't do a thing.
I see. How long have these spots been present, and have you noticed any bleeding or changes in their size lately?
They've been there for a few months now and seem to be getting a bit larger and crustier over time. I haven't noticed any bleeding, but they just won't heal no matter what I put on them.
That is helpful information. Do these spots ever itch or feel tender, and do you have any history of warts or exposure to HPV?
No, they don't itch or feel tender at all; they are completely painless. As for warts or HPV, I've never been told I had anything like that, though I've had many partners over the years.

I understand. Are the edges of these sores well-defined, and is the surrounding skin healthy or also affected? 

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
RESULTS: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.
Thank you for those results. Have you ever been exposed to arsenic or had significant sun exposure, and have you noticed any other similar patches on your body?

I haven't been around any arsenic that I know of, and I usually keep covered up from the sun. Aside from the spots on my finger and my penis, my skin is completely clear. I haven't been feeling sick or losing weight either, if that's what you're wondering.

I see. Have you noticed if any of your lymph nodes, particularly in your groin area, feel swollen or firm to the touch?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Bowen's disease (Squ
